DESCRIPTION.text:
This module was written to allow users to request products that are
frequently stocked by the company, to be transferred to their chosen
location.

USAGE.text:
\## Creation

- Go to 'Stock Requests / Stock Requests' and create a new Request.
- Indicate a product, quantity and location.
- Press 'Confirm'.

Upon confirmation the request will be evaluated using the procurement
rules for the selected location.

In case that transfers are created, the user will be able to access to
them from the button 'Transfers' available in the Stock Request.

\## Cancel

When the user cancels a Stock Request, the related pending stock moves
will be also cancelled.

CONFIGURE.text:
To configure this module:

- Go to Stock Requests \> Settings

Users should be assigned to the groups 'Stock Request / User' or 'Stock
Request / Manager'.

\## Group Stock Request / User

- Can see her/his own Stock Requests, and others that she/he's been
  granted permission to follow.
- Can create/update only her/his Stock Requests.

\## Group Stock Request / Manager

- Can fully manage all Stock Requests

ROADMAP.text:
There is no way to achieve Storck Request and Stock Request Orders. It
should be developed taking into account that only Cancel and Done stock
request can be archived.

It is also required to manage active field logically from Orders to SRs.

frequently stocked by the company, to be transferred to their chosen
location.

## USAGE

- Go to 'Stock Requests / Stock Requests' and create a new Request.
- Indicate a product, quantity and location.
- Press 'Confirm'.

Upon confirmation the request will be evaluated using the procurement
rules for the selected location.

In case that transfers are created, the user will be able to access to

\## Cancel

## CONFIGURE
To configure this module:

- Go to Stock Requests \> Settings

Users should be assigned to the groups 'Stock Request / User' or 'Stock
Request / Manager'.

\## Group Stock Request / Manager

## GITHUB ISSUES (selected)
### #119 [18.0][FIX] stock_request: count allocations after push steps (pr, closed, 2026)
With a two step route that uses a push rule , the stock request is linked to the first move. So:
- When the first step is done, the request is done, although the goods have not arrived yet.
- The push copies the first move, link included, so the second step counts the quantity again.
With this fix only the move that reaches the requested location counts. The push moves the link to the second move instead of copying it.

### #117 [18.0][FIX] stock_request: set done when partially delivered (pr, closed, 2026)
When a transfer is validated partially without a backorder, or the backorder is cancelled later, the request ends up Cancelled even if part of it was delivered. If all lines of an order end up like that, the order is Cancelled too.
This was changed in 6260722 to cancel requests whose moves get cancelled, which makes sense when nothing was delivered. Now a request is only Cancelled when nothing was delivered, otherwise it goes to Done. The cancelled quantity still shows what was missing.

### #116 [18.0][FIX] stock_request: split allocations with the move (pr, closed, 2026)
When a transfer is validated partially and a backorder is created, Qty In Progress keeps the full requested quantity instead of what's left. A request for 10 with 8 done still shows 10 in progress.
Now, when a move is split, the original move's allocations keep what stays on it and the new move gets the rest. This also covers the Split action on transfers. With exact quantities, a request is only closed when nothing is left in progress.

### #126 [18.0][FIX] stock_request: count returns and pushed moves once (pr, open, 2026)
Backport of the stock_request fixes of 20.0 (#108, #124, #125), already backported to 19.0 in #123, so the three versions share the same code.
- **Count returns and pushed moves once**: a return subtracts the quantity of the move it returns, also for internal transfers. When a push rule continues a move of the request, only the last move of the chain counts, so the request is not done before the goods reach its location. A copied allocation takes the quantity of the new move. A post-migration script limits the open allocations of existing backorders and recomputes the stored quantities of existing requests (version bumped to 18.0.1.2.0).
- **Keep split allocation qty unrounded**: when a move in a UoM other than the request's is split, or copied as a return or a push, its allocations are not rounded to the request UoM.
This replaces #119, which fixes the push steps with a different approach. Its tests also pass with this design (only the assertion on which move holds the allocation differs: here the first move keeps it and does not count it).
Migration checked on a database created with the current 18.0: a returned internal transfer goes from 20 done to 0; the other requests keep their quantities.

### #86 [18.0][IMP] stock_request: add default route in stock requests from order (pr, closed, 2025)
This was something that was in older versions but was removed (I believe it was accidentally when migrating to v16). See v15 [code](https://github.com/OCA/stock-logistics-warehouse/blob/15.0/stock_request/views/stock_request_order_views.xml#L123) with this implementation.
